mitigation_mechanism: Wooded buffers slow overland flow, add infiltration and woody debris that de-synchronises flood peaks.
caveats: Stated as valuable for moderate floods only; depends on woodland extent, location, age and density; mostly UK/temperate evidence. Narrative, no size: slight by rule.
justification: Cole et al. (2020) Agric. Ecosyst. Environ., review [source_id managing_buffer_strips_es_review_2020], PDF p.6: "Riparian woodlands appear to be particularly valuable to flood defence under moderate flooding, however, effectiveness is dependent not only on the extent and location of the woodland, but also on age and density, with mature woodlands being more effective due to their increased structural complexity and greater volume of deadwood en- tering watercourses (Dixon et al., 2015)."

mitigation_mechanism: Trees in buffer strips give livestock shade and shelter.
caveats: Narrative, no size. Applies where livestock graze next to the buffer.
justification: Cole et al. (2020) Agric. Ecosyst. Environ., review [source_id managing_buffer_strips_es_review_2020], PDF p.5: "Planting trees and shrubs in buffer strips also provides livestock with shelter from adverse weather (e.g. sun, rain and wind), alleviating tem- perature stress, and further benefitting production and welfare (Broom et al., 2013; Maseyk et al., 2017; Renaudeau et al., 2012)."
